dependencies: AUTHORITY: docs/ops/evaluate/EVALUATE_COMMERCIAL_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json (R2) must be MERGED and independently Opus-audited before any control here is written

OWNER RATIFICATIONS CONSUMED AND RESIDENT: docs/ops/evaluate/EVALUATE_OWNER_RATIFICATIONS_v1.0.0.json (HD-01..HD-16, via PR137 merge a3f3419e) and docs/ops/commercial/COMMERCIAL_V1_MICRO_RATIFICATIONS_v1.0.0.json (RAT-EV-02, RAT-EV-03, via PR146). All six R1 authority gaps are CLOSED; no control here waits on an adjudication.

EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY, NOT A BLOCKER: HD-12's bounded platform-support capability does not exist (PR145 measured OPEN and DRAFT). N-14 proves its ABSENCE rather than its behaviour, and must be rewritten when that capability is ratified and implemented.

BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE: exact leaf pathnames inside the two HD-11 route families are an implementation decision. N-20 tests the FAMILY CONTRACT (which subtrees and scopes are permitted) and must NOT be written to assert a specific invented URL.

known_conditions below is an EMPTY PLACEHOLDER, NOT a claim that the baseline carries none. The implementing node MUST re-derive it via pnpm ops:test-diff against its own HEAD before committing, per the schema's own instruction that known conditions are verified by machine and never re-adjudicated by prose.

postgres_requirements.rationale: Twelve RLS_SECURITY_INVARIANTS and seven NO_SUPERADMIN_BYPASS_CONTROLS are properties of POLICY EVALUATION, not of SQL text. Grepping a migration for the absence of current_user_is_super_admin proves the string is absent; it does NOT prove that a super_admin principal cannot read a row, that a DECIDED row rejects UPDATE, that OBJ-4 rejects UPDATE and DELETE outright, that UPDATE/DELETE denial-by-omission actually denies, that a no-organization principal sees zero rows rather than all rows, or that FORCE RLS applies to the table owner. Those require a real PostgreSQL instance with real roles, via pnpm db:audit:disposable against the disposable harness — never staging, never production, never the canonical local stack.

sentinels.purpose: A fictional, unmistakable decision-rationale string planted as the decision_rationale of a divergent decision. Its appearance anywhere in audit_logs.before_json or audit_logs.after_json proves the NSB-04 payload contract was violated and that tenant decision content became readable through a relation whose SELECT policy carries the platform-superadmin bypass. Never a real credential and never real tenant text.
A fictional governed-N/A rationale string, planted the same way, proving na_rationale text likewise never reaches an audit payload.

A fictional score-rationale marker planted on the FIRST version of a criterion response and never reused on its replacement. Its survival after the response is superseded proves RAT-EV-03's traceability floor is real — the prior action's row still exists with its own actor, role and timestamp. Its disappearance proves an overwriting upsert was built instead.

positive_controls.description: EV-01 arithmetic: an evaluation whose criteria mix SCORED and governed NOT_APPLICABLE current responses yields a Score in which every NOT_APPLICABLE criterion is absent from BOTH numerator and denominator. Proven by a fixture where excluding-from-both, excluding-from-numerator-only, and scoring-N/A-as-zero each produce a DIFFERENT number, so the test distinguishes the ratified rule from the two plausible wrong ones.

Determinism (HD-01): the scoring function called twice with identical (criteria, responses) returns byte-identical results, and its module imports nothing from db, no fetch, no Date, no Math.random and no process.env — asserted structurally over the module source, not only behaviourally.

DecisionPolicy totality (HD-03): for a published policy, every representable COMPUTED score — including each band boundary value approached from both sides — maps to exactly one member of ('approve','approve_with_conditions','reject'). No score yields zero outcomes and none yields two.

Default designated decider (HD-05): an evaluation created with no explicit designated_decision_role carries 'organization_admin', and an actor whose role in THAT organization is organization_admin completes T5 successfully.

Designated impact_manager (HD-05): an evaluation explicitly designated to impact_manager is decidable by an impact_manager of that organization, proving the decision set genuinely has two members rather than organization_admin plus a comment.

Snapshot atomicity: a successful T5 writes all nine snapshot values — score_snapshot, score_status_snapshot, recommended_outcome_snapshot, decision_policy_hash_snapshot, decision_outcome, decision_rationale (where applicable), decided_by, decided_by_role, decided_at — in the same transaction as the state change, and the evaluation.decision_recorded audit row exists in that same transaction. A partial snapshot is asserted to be absent, not merely unobserved.

Snapshot is read, not recomputed (HD-06): after a decision is recorded, publishing a NEW template version with a different DecisionPolicy leaves the decided evaluation's rendered recommended outcome and derived divergence UNCHANGED, because both come from recommended_outcome_snapshot. This is the control that catches a read path which recomputes from the current template.

Archive from every pre-DECIDED state (HD-08): T6 (from DRAFT), T7 (from IN_PROGRESS) and T8 (from READY_FOR_DECISION) each succeed and each emit evaluation.archived. All three are exercised, proving ARCHIVED is reachable from the whole pre-decision region rather than only from DRAFT.

Template version identity and pinning: (template_id, version) and (template_id, ordinal) are unique; definition_hash and decision_policy_hash are computed server-side over a canonical serialization and are stable across recomputation; and an evaluation that pinned version N is unaffected in every observable way by the publication of version N+1 or by the retirement of its container.

Stella-independence (SB-07): with the Stella provider unreachable, disabled and unconfigured in three separate arrangements, every transition T1 through T8 still completes. Evaluate is proven functional without AI rather than merely believed to be.

Traceability floor over superseded responses (RAT-EV-03): a criterion response is recorded by actor A, then superseded by actor B. Afterwards BOTH rows exist with their own recorded_by, recorded_by_role, ordinal and recorded_at; the EVAL-SUPERSEDED-RESPONSE-CANARY planted on the first row is still readable; the current projection resolves to B's row; and A's row is unchanged. This is the control that distinguishes the append-only model from R1's overwriting upsert.

Template draft/publish/retire as three distinct authorized acts (HD-09): an impact_manager drafts a template version; an organization_admin publishes it; an organization_admin retires the container. All three succeed, each emits its own audit key (evaluation_template_version.created, .published, evaluation_template.retired), and each records its own actor and role at action.

No mandatory person-inequality (RAT-EV-03): ONE organization_admin records every criterion response, submits for decision, and records the decision on the same evaluation. The journey completes successfully. Proves Commercial V1 does not enforce distinct natural persons across author, reviewer and decision maker — and the same test asserts the full traceability floor is still populated on every action that person performed.

The criterion-edit set admits all three of its members (RAT-EV-02): analyst, impact_manager and organization_admin each successfully create and edit a criterion response on a pre-lock evaluation, exercised individually. analyst is included deliberately and explicitly — it is the member no hierarchy-threshold expression of the DECISION set would ever admit, so its positive path must be proven, not assumed.

negative_controls.description: super_admin is REFUSED as a decider at two layers (HD-05): canDecideEvaluation('super_admin') returns false, and a T5 attempt by a super_admin principal against an organization_admin-designated evaluation is refused server-side and audited as evaluation.decision_refused. The single most important control in the manifest — the exact violation the hierarchy shorthand introduces invisibly.

Zero denominator (HD-02): an evaluation in which EVERY criterion has a current governed NOT_APPLICABLE response yields score_status 'SCORE_NOT_COMPUTABLE', produces NO recommended outcome at all (not a defaulted one), and REFUSES T5 with an audited refusal. Additionally asserts the returned score is neither 0, nor -1, nor null-coerced, nor NaN, nor Infinity (ZD-03).

No standing platform-superadmin bypass (HD-12): the Evaluate migration contains zero occurrences of current_user_is_super_admin, AND — proven against real PostgreSQL — a super_admin principal with no membership in the target organization reads ZERO rows from every Evaluate relation. Additionally asserts no Evaluate content row exists in domain_object_versions, so DRR-01's refusal is enforced and not merely documented.

Audit payload contract (NSB-04): after a divergent decision whose decision_rationale is EVAL-RATIONALE-CANARY and whose governed-N/A rationale is EVAL-NA-RATIONALE-CANARY, neither sentinel appears anywhere in audit_logs.before_json or audit_logs.after_json, while the audit row still carries enough prior state to reconstruct the transition (satisfying the fail-closed logger's FIBC-040 contract). Proves the contract and its reconciliation together, not one at the other's expense.

Divergence rationale is mandatory (HD-06): a T5 attempt whose decision_outcome differs from recommended_outcome_snapshot and whose decision_rationale is missing, null, empty or whitespace-only is REFUSED server-side; and the same row is UNREPRESENTABLE at the database, proven by a direct INSERT/UPDATE bypassing the action being rejected by the CHECK constraint.

No override path for decisions (NSB-05): an actor whose role is in EVALUATE_DECISION_ROLES but does NOT match the evaluation's designated_decision_role is REFUSED at T5. Additionally, a repository-wide assertion proves no exported action, route handler, script or database function outside the single authorized decision path writes decision_outcome, decided_by or decided_at — the control that proves an ABSENCE rather than testing a presence.

UNANSWERED is not governed N/A: an evaluation with at least one criterion carrying NO response row is REFUSED at T3, and its criteria are NOT excluded from the denominator. Proven against the adjacent case — the same criterion with an explicit NOT_APPLICABLE plus rationale — which DOES pass T3 and IS excluded, so the two cases are demonstrably distinguished.

Narrow FIB run-review surface preserved (HD-15): no Evaluate module imports from or writes to lib/pipeline/methodology-review.ts, lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts or the sroi_run_reviews relation; assertRunMethodologyApprovalAllowed, isInReviewSet and canApproveRunMethodology are byte-unchanged; the existing methodology-review suite is green; and no Evaluate relation carries a foreign key to any FIBIU-19 or FIBIU-20 object. Proves broad Evaluate is structurally Wave3-independent AND that the narrow surface was not annexed — the two halves of HD-15 in one control.

The other three forbidden decision roles (HD-05): analyst, reviewer and viewer are each REFUSED at T5, individually and explicitly. Enumerated separately from N-01 because a hierarchy-threshold implementation refuses these three CORRECTLY while admitting super_admin — so a test that only checks 'low roles are denied' passes on the broken implementation.

super_admin is REFUSED from criterion editing (RAT-EV-02): canEditEvaluationCriterionResponse('super_admin') returns false, and a T2 attempt by a super_admin principal on a pre-lock evaluation is refused server-side and audited as evaluation_criterion_response.edit_refused. RAT-EV-02 excludes super_admin from the edit set by name; this is the control that proves it, and it is the one a hasRole(role,'analyst') implementation fails while passing everything else.

reviewer and viewer are REFUSED from criterion editing (RAT-EV-02): each is refused individually at T2. Additionally a structural assertion proves neither Evaluate role set is derived from isInReviewSet or from REVIEW_ROLES — reviewer is a member of the repository's review set but is excluded from BOTH Evaluate sets, so deriving either from isInReviewSet would admit it in one move.

The two Evaluate role sets are NOT the same set: in one test, an analyst SUCCEEDS at editing a criterion response and is REFUSED at recording a decision on the same evaluation. Proves the criterion-edit set and the decision set are distinct and that neither was collapsed into the other — a single shared helper cannot satisfy both halves of this control.

role_at_action is stored, never derived (TRACEABILITY_FLOOR): a criterion response is recorded by an impact_manager whose organization role is then CHANGED to analyst. The stored recorded_by_role still reads 'impact_manager'. Likewise a decision recorded by an organization_admin whose role later changes still reports 'organization_admin' in decided_by_role. Proves the role is a snapshot of the act and not a join to current membership.

No platform-support access path exists (HD-12, NSB-07): a repository-wide assertion proves no Evaluate action, route handler, policy, view or database function grants read or write on Evaluate content to a platform principal, support role, operator capability or impersonation mechanism. Proves an ABSENCE. Must be rewritten — not deleted — when a bounded support capability is ratified and implemented; PR145 is measured OPEN and DRAFT and supplies nothing today.

A defective DecisionPolicy is REFUSED AT PUBLICATION (HD-03): three separate policies are each rejected by the publish path — one whose bands are UNORDERED in the stored policy, one with a GAP, one with an OVERLAP — plus a fourth carrying a fallback branch. Refusal is at publication, not at evaluation, because HD-03 constrains the stored policy inside the immutable version.

Template draft and publish/retire roles do not leak into each other (HD-09): an impact_manager is REFUSED at publishing and REFUSED at retiring; an organization_admin is REFUSED at drafting; and super_admin is REFUSED at all three. Four refusals, asserted individually, so a single collapsed canManageTemplate helper fails this control whichever role it settled on.

The governing lock is real and DECIDED is terminal: after T5, a criterion-response create and a criterion-response edit are each REFUSED and audited; T5-then-archive is REFUSED (HD-08); every other transition out of DECIDED is REFUSED; and — proven against real PostgreSQL — an UPDATE against a DECIDED row, any UPDATE against OBJ-4, and any DELETE against OBJ-3 or OBJ-4 are all denied by RLS even for a member of the owning organization. Separately asserts a criterion edit on an ARCHIVED evaluation is refused too, which is a different refusal with a different reason.

Tenant isolation by predicate (RLS-11): a principal who is a member of organization B reads ZERO Evaluate rows belonging to organization A; and a principal resolving to NO organization reads ZERO rows rather than ALL rows. The second half is the important one — an ambient or null scope has previously resolved to GLOBAL rather than to refusal in this repository.

Template version immutability (RLS-04): UPDATE of criteria_json, decision_policy_json, version, ordinal or either hash on a published evaluation_template_versions row is denied by policy omission AND independently rejected by the uellix_forbid_mutation trigger; DELETE is denied; and the ONLY permitted mutation is the single write-once NULL-to-value publication transition, which is proven to succeed once and be refused a second time. Both defence layers are asserted separately so removing either one is visible. Also asserts a version with zero criteria cannot be published (ZD-06).

Route-family contract without inventing a pathname (HD-11): a structural assertion over the route tree proves every Evaluate page lives under either the project subtree or the organization subtree, that no Evaluate route exists outside app/app/**, that no Evaluate route is public or anonymous, that no template surface appears at project scope and no evaluation surface at organization scope, and that NAV_LINKS gained no Evaluate entry. Written against subtree membership and scope, deliberately NOT against any specific leaf URL, because exact pathnames are a bounded implementation choice.

Stella cannot produce the authoritative recommendation (HD-01, SB-03): a Stella advisor response returning an outcome-shaped suggestion that DIFFERS from the deterministic recommended outcome leaves recommended_outcome_snapshot equal to the SYSTEM value, leaves the derived divergence computed from the SYSTEM value only, and the Stella suggestion appears in no Evaluate column. Additionally a structural assertion proves the scoring and decision-policy functions accept no Stella-derived argument, and that OBJ-3 has no stella_* column — so SB-04 is verified as structural, not conventional. Also asserts stella_role is 'advisor' and pipeline_step is exactly 'evaluate_analysis' (HD-07) and that no new stella_role value was added.

mutation_controls.description: Replace the decision predicate with the hierarchy shorthand — canDecideEvaluation(role) = hasRole(role, 'organization_admin') — and N-01 MUST turn RED while N-09 stays GREEN. The asymmetry is the proof: a suite that goes fully green under this mutation is only testing that low roles are denied. Mutates the implementation to reintroduce the real hazard (7 existing helpers use that exact shape), so it is a strengthening mutation and not a weakened test.

Add OR current_user_is_super_admin() to the Evaluate SELECT policies and N-03 MUST turn RED at BOTH of its halves — the text assertion and the real-PostgreSQL read. If only the text half goes red, the RLS probe is not actually exercising a super_admin principal and N-03 is half-vacuous.

Make the scoring function return 0 with score_status 'COMPUTED' when the denominator is zero, and N-02 MUST turn RED. If N-02 stays green it is asserting on the status field alone and would not catch a sentinel number reaching the DecisionPolicy bands.

Add a second write path to decision_outcome — an admin action, a script, or a direct repository helper — and N-06 MUST turn RED. If it stays green, N-06 is testing the authorized path rather than proving the absence of others, and NSB-05 is unproven.

Add an UPDATE policy permitting a snapshot column to be changed on a DECIDED row, and BOTH P-06 and N-17 MUST turn RED. Separately: mutate a stored snapshot value out-of-band and assert the snapshot-versus-recomputation comparison detects it, which is what gives the deliberate score redundancy its purpose.

Add a stored divergence boolean column, switch the read model to read it instead of deriving, and set it to disagree with the two snapshots — P-07 MUST turn RED. Proves the derivation is genuinely a derivation and that no consumer reads a cached divergence.

Revert OBJ-4 to R1's overwriting upsert — UNIQUE (evaluation_id, criterion_key) with an UPDATE on conflict — and BOTH P-11 and N-13 MUST turn RED, with the EVAL-SUPERSEDED-RESPONSE-CANARY provably gone. This is the mutation that proves RAT-EV-03's traceability floor is enforced by the model rather than described by it; if the suite stays green the append-only correction is decorative.

Collapse canDraftEvaluationTemplate, canPublishEvaluateTemplateVersion and canRetireEvaluateTemplate into one canManageTemplate helper — under EITHER role choice — and N-16 MUST turn RED. With {impact_manager} it admits impact_manager to publishing, which HD-09 forbids; with {organization_admin} it denies impact_manager drafting, which HD-09 permits. Both collapses are required to be caught, so the control is run twice.

Replace the criterion-edit predicate with hasRole(role, 'analyst') — the shape an implementer would naturally reach for, since analyst is the lowest-ranked member of the edit set — and N-10 MUST turn RED while N-11 and P-14 stay GREEN. This mutation is correct for five of six roles: it admits analyst, impact_manager and organization_admin and correctly denies reviewer and viewer. It is wrong for exactly the one role RAT-EV-02 excludes by name. A suite that survives it entirely is not testing RAT-EV-02 at all.

Remove the publication-time band-order validation while leaving the evaluator able to sort bands before evaluating, and N-15's unordered case MUST turn RED while its gap and overlap cases stay GREEN. The asymmetry proves HD-03 is enforced over the STORED policy and not merely satisfied by a tolerant evaluator — an evaluator that produces the right answer from an unordered stored policy still violates HD-03.

Replace recorded_by_role and decided_by_role reads with a join to current organization membership, and N-13 MUST turn RED. If it stays green the test is asserting the column exists rather than that it is a snapshot, and a role change after the act would silently falsify the traceability record.
